cards.statement: This guide is a regular .shrimp file, like any other.
cards.explanation: It's made just like the files you save, and it opened into this browser like one. Change it, add your own courses or delete it all. Download saves it as a .shrimp file of your own.

cards.title: What holds what, biggest first
cards.explanation: Your library is everything here, kept as one .shrimp file. Make a course for each class, like Biology, and a quiz for each chapter.
At the bottom of the sidebar. It opens the new course, ready for its name.
A tile on the course page. It opens Edit quiz, where you name it and add cards.
Select the title at the top of its page and type. A quiz is renamed the same way, in Edit quiz.
Beside Shrimply Study, top left. Select it again to bring the sidebar back.

cards.statement: The {sidebar} lists your courses and quizzes. The {top row} shows where you are: select {Home} to see all your courses.
explanation: Select any part of it to go back there. Every page has its own address, so you can bookmark it.

cards.statement: Pick a look in the {Theme} menu, under New course.
cards.explanation: This browser remembers it. It isn't saved in your file.

cards.statement: A deleted course can be brought back.
cards.explanation: Danger zone, at the bottom of a course's page, deletes it, and a quiz's is at the bottom of Edit quiz. Both ask first, and can't be undone.

cards.question: Which button on a quiz's page studies it?
cards.explanation: It sits beside Edit quiz. The study options under it pick how you study.

cards.question: Which of these are themes?
cards.explanation: There are seven, all dark: Calm, Neon arcade, Underwater, Enchanted forest, Sassy unicorn, Quizlet and Kahoot.

cards.title: Add a card, start to finish
cards.explanation: Edit quiz is on the quiz page, and Add new card under the cards has a button for each kind. Done drops empty cards; a half-filled one turns red and keeps you here. To move a step in a sequence like this one, drag it by its grip or press Alt+Up or Alt+Down.

cards.statement: {Enter} goes to the next box, and from the last one to a new card. {Shift+Enter} starts a new line.
explanation: In a list of answers or steps, Enter in the last box adds one, and in an empty last box leaves the list.

cards.term: How do you name a card's sides?
cards.explanation: Front / Back, Question / Answer like this card, Term / Definition and more. New type makes your own, and its pencil renames or deletes it. New cards take the sides of the last one.

cards.statement: Select words, then {Mark as blank} or press {Ctrl+B}. It works {inside {a blank}} too.
explanation: Each blank is asked on its own, with the rest of the sentence as the clue, and can have its own explanation, like this one.

cards.question: What does a choice question offer when you study it?
cards.explanation: Fill in its Right answers and Wrong answers. With one correct answer you pick it; with several, like here, you pick all of them, then Check.
Beside each side, statement, question or title. Or paste or drop an image on the field. Select the thumbnail to replace it, or its ✕ to remove it.

cards.term: Remove an answer, step or explanation
cards.explanation: At the end of its box, while you point at it or type in it. Explanation, at the top of a card, adds one back.
Beside Done. Paste a Quizlet export or spreadsheet rows, one card per line, check the preview, then pick a group.

cards.statement: This icon on a card removes its image.
cards.explanation: It deletes the whole card. An image's own ✕ removes just the image.

cards.question: What does a group change when you study?
right: Wrong options come from it first
cards.explanation: Put cards that are easy to mix up in one group, so multiple choice offers them against each other. New group is under the cards, and a card's group menu moves it. Select a group's dot to change its color.

cards.title: One round, start to finish
cards.explanation: The mode, side and order you pick on the quiz page are remembered. Esc leaves a round. The results list every answer, with filters for Missed, Right and Marked.

cards.statement: Press {Space} to flip a flashcard, the {number keys} to pick an option, {Enter} to check and go on, and {Esc} to leave.
explanation: Then 1 for Didn't know, or 2 for Knew it.

cards.statement: With Question side set to Back, you see the back and answer with the front.
cards.explanation: Mixed picks a side for each card. Other kinds of cards ignore it and show their own text.

cards.question: What doesn't count when you type an answer?
cards.explanation: For a typo or another correct wording, select I was right: it counts, and the results mark it as yours.
On the card, in the results too, and on the quiz page. The change shows right away.
On a flashcard or an option, rest the pointer on it until its border closes. Esc or any click closes it.

cards.definition: Flip, then say if you knew it
cards.explanation: Select the card or press Space to flip it.
It needs at least 2 cards. A choice question offers its own answers, and a sequence is dragged into order.
A sequence is asked one step at a time. A true or false card still gets two buttons.

cards.question: Where do the wrong options in multiple choice come from?
cards.explanation: From the same group first. Pick a wrong one, and it says which card it belongs to.
At the top, or Ctrl+S. Everything goes in one .shrimp file you can keep, send or open on another device. A * in the tab title means unsaved changes.
At the top. It replaces the library in this browser, and asks first when you have unsaved changes.

cards.statement: The top of the sidebar says where the open library is: {On this device}, {Your Google Drive} or {Only in this browser}.
explanation: A .shrimp file you opened or downloaded.
Or Someone else's Google Drive for one shared with you. Signed out, it says Shared on Google Drive or On Google Drive.
In no file yet: download it or save it to Drive to keep it.

cards.statement: Shrimply Study keeps your cards on its own server.
cards.explanation: It has none. Your cards stay in this browser, which keeps a copy between visits, and in the files you save: a .shrimp file or your own Google Drive.

cards.question: How do you start an empty library?
cards.explanation: It asks first. Save this one first, or its unsaved changes are lost.

cards.title: Share a library
cards.explanation: Google Drive is at the top. Anyone with the link can open the library and study it, with no sign-in.
At the top, or Ctrl+S, once the library is in your Drive. It asks first if the file changed on another device.
In the sidebar, on a library shared with you. It asks first, as it replaces the courses here.
Sign in there and open it from your list in the Google Drive dialog. The share link or the .shrimp file works too.

cards.question: What can someone with your link do?
right: Change it in their own browser
Save a copy to their Drive
cards.explanation: Only you save into your file. The app only sees the files it saved for you, never the rest of your Drive.

cards.title: Make a library by hand or with an AI
cards.explanation: Rename the .shrimp file to .zip to unzip it, and the new zip back to .shrimp. Zip the files themselves, not a folder around them. A sequence like this one is "type": "sequence", a "title" and its "steps" in order.

cards.question: What stops a file from opening?
right: A field these cards don't list
cards.explanation: Ids and unknown fields are refused, and the message names the spot, like courses[0].quizzes[1].cards[3]. Optional fields can be left out, and "quizzes" and "cards" can be empty lists.
"version" is 2. An optional "sideTypes" lists your own side names, like [["Task", "Where to click"]] in this guide.
No two courses can share a name. Case, spaces and punctuation don't count.
No two quizzes in a course can share a name. "cards" holds the cards in no group.
lagoon, coral, sky, sand, moss, rose, clay or slate. Without one, like the Cards group here, it takes the first one not in use.
Optional: "sides" like ["Question", "Answer"] (Front and Back when left out), "termImage", "definitionImage" and "explanation". All text is plain, and \n is a line break.

cards.term: Which field shows this picture on the front?
cards.explanation: "termImage": "shrimp.svg" names images/shrimp.svg in the zip, a png, jpg, gif, webp, avif or svg. "definitionImage" is for the back, and the other kinds have one "image". Cards can share a file.

cards.statement: Each {blank} in a "statement" goes in {braces}, and a blank can hold {another {blank}}.
explanation: A fill-in-the-blank card is "type": "cloze" and a "statement", with optional "image" and "explanation".
Write \{ and \} for plain braces and \\ for a backslash. In library.json each backslash is doubled.
Blanks count in the order of their {, so this is blank 4. With several blanks, "explanation" is a list with one entry per blank, and "" for none.

cards.explanation: Without quotes: "answer": true. A true or false card is "type": "true-false", a "statement" and an "answer", with optional "image" and "explanation".

cards.question: Besides "type": "choice", which fields does a choice question need?
cards.explanation: "right" and "wrong" are lists of texts; with several right ones, you pick all. "image" and "explanation" are optional.
